items.title: AzuraCast before 0.23.6 contains a code injection vulnerability in the remote relay password field due to incomplete migration from the vulnerable cleanUpString method to toRawS...
items.summary: AzuraCast before 0.23.6 contains a code injection vulnerability in the remote relay password field due to incomplete migration from the vulnerable cleanUpString method to toRawString. Attackers with RemoteRelays station permission can inject nested Liquidsoap interpolation syntax to execute arbitrary code in the Liquidsoap process, disclose internal API keys, or disrupt station operation.

llm_summary.summary_zh: AzuraCast 是一款开源的网络电台/流媒体管理与自动化播出平台，其在 0.23.6 之前的版本中存在一处代码注入漏洞。根因是开发团队进行输入处理 API 迁移时留下了不完整的改造：早期版本使用 cleanUpString 方法对用户可控字符串进行清理与转义，后续改为 toRawString 以保留原始字符，但『远程中继（Remote Relays）』配置项的密码字段没有被同步迁移到安全路径，导致该字段的用户输入在进入下游生成流程时缺少必要的过滤。该字段的取值最终会被拼接进 Liquidsoap 的脚本/配置内容中，而 Liquidsoap 支持插值语法（形如 #{...} 的表达式求值）。攻击者只要持有站点的 RemoteRelays 权限（即一个已通过认证、具备中继配置管理能力的账号，对应 CVSS 向量中的 PR:L），便可在此密码字段中写入嵌套的 Liquidsoap 插值表达式，使 Liquidsoap 进程在解析配置时对表达式求值，从而在 Liquidsoap 运行上下文中执行任意代码。成功利用后可导致三类后果：一是读取并外泄 AzuraCast 的内部 API 密钥等敏感凭据；二是篡改播出配置、劫持或中断电台的正常播送；三是破坏服务可用性。CVSS 3.1 评分为 8.8（AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H），属于高危。当前输入数据中未提供 EPSS 分数，漏洞未列入 CISA KEV，也未标注在野利用信息。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 仅需 RemoteRelays 这类较低权限的已认证账号，即可在 Liquidsoap 进程内执行任意代码并窃取内部 API 密钥，CVSS 高达 8.8；管理面板若暴露在互联网上，风险尤为突出。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 影响所有 AzuraCast < 0.23.6 的部署，尤其是向多名管理员或节目制作人开放 RemoteRelays 权限、且管理面板可被外部访问的实例。机密性（内部 API 密钥泄露）、完整性（注入恶意脚本/配置）与可用性（播出中断或被劫持）均受高度影响。

items.why_it_matters: 仅需 RemoteRelays 这类较低权限的已认证账号，即可在 Liquidsoap 进程内执行任意代码并窃取内部 API 密钥，CVSS 高达 8.8；管理面板若暴露在互联网上，风险尤为突出。

items.title: AzuraCast before 0.23.6 contains a missing permission check vulnerability in the GET /api/station/{station_id}/file/{id}/play endpoint that allows authenticated users to downloa...
items.summary: AzuraCast before 0.23.6 contains a missing permission check vulnerability in the GET /api/station/{station_id}/file/{id}/play endpoint that allows authenticated users to download media files from any station. Attackers can enumerate media files using sequential IDs and exfiltrate the complete media library of stations they lack permissions for.

llm_summary.summary_zh: AzuraCast 是一款开源的网络电台（流媒体）管理与自动化播出平台，广泛用于自建电台、社区广播与多租户托管场景。该漏洞影响 0.23.6 之前的所有版本：位于 GET /api/station/{station_id}/file/{id}/play 的媒体播放/下载接口缺少必要的权限校验，服务端既没有验证发起请求的账号是否有权访问 station_id 所指向的电台，也没有校验 file id 与目标电台之间的归属关系。任何持有有效登录凭据的低权限用户（例如仅被授权管理自己电台的普通账号或受限角色），都可以把 URL 中的 station_id 与 file id 替换为任意值，从而下载其他电台的媒体文件。由于文件 ID 采用顺序递增的整数，攻击者不需要猜测即可通过遍历枚举出目标实例上所有电台的全部媒体内容，造成跨电台、跨租户的数据越权读取与批量外泄。该缺陷属于典型的 IDOR / 缺失授权（Broken Access Control）问题。CVSS 3.1 基础评分为 6.5（中等），向量为 AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N，即远程可利用、复杂度低、需要低权限、无需用户交互，仅影响机密性但影响程度为高，不涉及完整性与可用性。官方已在 0.23.6 版本中修复该问题。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 多租户或共享部署下，任意低权限账号即可批量拖走全实例的媒体库，属于典型 IDOR/越权读取缺陷。利用门槛极低而数据泄露面很大，修复成本低，应优先纳入补丁窗口。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 成功利用可导致跨电台媒体库被完整枚举并下载，造成知识产权、独家音频内容与业务数据泄露；受影响系统自身不被篡改或中断，但机密性受损，且大规模自动化遍历难以被常规监控察觉。

items.why_it_matters: 多租户或共享部署下，任意低权限账号即可批量拖走全实例的媒体库，属于典型 IDOR/越权读取缺陷。利用门槛极低而数据泄露面很大，修复成本低，应优先纳入补丁窗口。

items.title: AzuraCast before 0.23.6 lacks RequireInternalConnection middleware on the Liquidsoap API endpoint and incorrectly derives the AutoDJ flag from header presence rather than valida...
items.summary: AzuraCast before 0.23.6 lacks RequireInternalConnection middleware on the Liquidsoap API endpoint and incorrectly derives the AutoDJ flag from header presence rather than validated value. Users with View station permission can inject arbitrary now-playing metadata, disrupt live broadcasts, and disclose filesystem paths.

llm_summary.summary_zh: AzuraCast 是一款开源的网络广播电台管理与自动化播出平台，其内部通过 Liquidsoap API 端点实现后端与 AutoDJ（自动播出）组件之间的通信，该端点本应只接受来自本机或受信内部网络的调用。在 0.23.6 之前的版本中存在两处缺陷：其一，该端点未挂载 RequireInternalConnection 中间件，导致内部接口没有强制校验请求来源，缺少网络层面的访问控制；其二，程序判断请求是否来自 AutoDJ 时，仅依据某个请求头“是否存在”，而没有对其取值进行合法性校验，即把头部的存在性当作可信凭据。两处缺陷叠加后，任何已通过身份认证、仅拥有 "View station"（查看电台）这一最低读取权限的用户，都能向该内部端点发送构造请求，从而向电台注入任意的正在播放（now-playing）元数据，干扰正在进行的直播广播内容，并造成服务器文件系统路径信息泄露，为后续更深入的探测提供线索。该漏洞的 CVSS 3.1 向量为 AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L，评分 6.3，属中危：可远程利用、攻击复杂度低、需要低权限账号、无需用户交互，对机密性、完整性与可用性影响均为低。目前 NVD 元数据中未标注已被列入 KEV 或在野利用。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 内部通信端点缺少来源校验且凭据判断逻辑错误，使仅具“查看电台”权限的最低权限用户即可篡改直播内容、干扰播出并泄露服务器路径，暴露了内网接口默认可信这一常见设计缺陷。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 已认证低权限用户可注入任意 now-playing 元数据、扰乱直播广播，并获取文件系统路径信息；对机密性、完整性、可用性均造成低度影响，评分 6.3（中危）。

items.why_it_matters: 内部通信端点缺少来源校验且凭据判断逻辑错误，使仅具“查看电台”权限的最低权限用户即可篡改直播内容、干扰播出并泄露服务器路径，暴露了内网接口默认可信这一常见设计缺陷。

items.title: In AzuraCast before 0.23.8, the public On-Demand download endpoint fails to verify playlist-level access controls, allowing unauthenticated users to download media files exclude...
items.summary: In AzuraCast before 0.23.8, the public On-Demand download endpoint fails to verify playlist-level access controls, allowing unauthenticated users to download media files excluded from On-Demand-enabled playlists. Attackers can bypass the station operator's intended access restrictions by directly requesting media via the download endpoint using valid media identifiers, exposing private or restricted audio content.

llm_summary.summary_zh: AzuraCast 是一套开源的网络电台 / 流媒体自托管平台, 提供直播、自动播放列表 (AutoDJ) 与按需点播 (On-Demand) 下载等功能。CVE-2026-100853 指出在其 0.23.8 之前的版本中, 面向公众开放的 On-Demand 下载端点未能对播放列表级别的访问控制进行校验, 导致权限判定被绕过。按照设计, 站点运营者可以把某些媒体文件排除在启用了 On-Demand 的播放列表之外, 从而限制其可获取范围; 但该下载端点在处理请求时只依据媒体标识符查找并返回文件, 没有回头验证该媒体是否真的属于当前允许点播的播放列表, 也没有验证请求者身份。于是未认证的匿名用户只要掌握或猜中合法的媒体标识符, 就能直接向该端点发起请求, 拿到本应被排除在外的音频文件。这是一类典型的访问控制缺失 / 越权信息泄露 (CWE-284 / CWE-639 类似模式) 问题, 其直接后果是私有或受限的音频内容被非授权读取, 可能涉及未公开的节目素材、内部音源或受版权限制的内容。利用难度被评估为偏高 (CVSS 3.1 向量 AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), 即网络可达、无需认证与交互, 但需要攻击者获得有效媒体标识符, 因此机密性影响为高, 完整性与可用性不受影响, 综合基础分 5.9。官方已在 0.23.8 版本中修复。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 匿名用户可绕过播放列表级访问控制, 直接下载被运营者刻意排除的音频内容, 造成私有或受限媒体泄露。虽然需要有效媒体标识符、利用门槛偏高, 但无需任何认证, 暴露在公网的 AzuraCast 电台实例应尽快核查。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 机密性影响为高: 未认证攻击者可读取并下载被标记为不可点播 / 受限的音频文件, 可能导致未公开节目素材、内部音源或受版权保护内容外泄; 完整性与可用性不受影响, 无远程代码执行风险。当前无 KEV 与在野利用标注。

items.why_it_matters: 匿名用户可绕过播放列表级访问控制, 直接下载被运营者刻意排除的音频内容, 造成私有或受限媒体泄露。虽然需要有效媒体标识符、利用门槛偏高, 但无需任何认证, 暴露在公网的 AzuraCast 电台实例应尽快核查。

items.title: AzuraCast through 0.23.x contains a command injection vulnerability in the Liquidsoap config generation for live recording that fails to quote the streamer username in process.r...
items.summary: AzuraCast through 0.23.x contains a command injection vulnerability in the Liquidsoap config generation for live recording that fails to quote the streamer username in process.run calls. Authenticated station users with Streamers and Profile permissions can set a username containing shell metacharacters and trigger command execution as the Liquidsoap process user when recording closes.

llm_summary.summary_zh: CVE-2026-100852 是 AzuraCast 0.23.x 及更早版本中的一个命令注入漏洞，CVSS 3.1 评分为 8.8（向量 AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H），属于高危级别。AzuraCast 是一套开源的、可自托管的网络电台管理与流媒体控制平台，其音频播放与录制编排依赖外部组件 Liquidsoap。该平台会根据管理后台中的配置，自动为 Liquidsoap 生成配置文件；在涉及“实时录制（live recording）”功能的配置生成逻辑中，代码把主播（streamer）的用户名直接拼接进 Liquidsoap 的 process.run 调用，却没有对该用户名做引号包裹或转义处理。Liquidsoap 在执行 process.run 时会通过 shell 解释执行传入的字符串，因此当用户名中包含 shell 元字符（如分号、反引号、命令替换与管道等）时，这些字符会被 shell 当作语法解析，从而注入并执行任意命令。触发该漏洞需要攻击者已经通过身份认证，并具备 Streamers（主播管理）与 Profile（个人资料）两项权限——这类权限通常授予电台运营人员或主播账号，而非匿名访客。攻击者只需在用户名等可控字段中植入恶意字符，随后当该次录制结束、Liquidsoap 处理收尾逻辑时，注入的命令即以运行 Liquidsoap 服务的操作系统用户身份被实际执行。这构成从低权限 Web 应用账号向宿主操作系统账户的越权跳转，攻击者可借此读取或篡改音频文件与配置、窃取凭证、建立持久化，并可能以该服务账户为跳板向同主机或内网其他资产横向移动。NVD 元数据未提供具体受影响产品版本清单与厂商信息，但依据描述可判断影响范围为 AzuraCast 0.23.x 及其之前版本。当前该 CVE 未列入 CISA KEV，元数据中也没有标记已知在野利用或已武器化，因此应将其视为需要尽快修复的高危缺陷，而非已确认被活跃利用的事件。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 拥有主播与资料权限的低权限已认证用户即可借助恶意用户名，在录制结束时以 Liquidsoap 服务账户身份执行任意命令，实现从 Web 账号到宿主系统的越权与横向移动。CVSS 8.8 且利用条件明确，自托管电台场景中该类后台账号通常较易获得。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 成功的命令注入会导致以 Liquidsoap 进程用户身份执行任意系统命令，可读取/篡改音频与配置数据、窃取凭证、植入持久化后门，并可能以该主机为跳板向同网段其他系统横向渗透。未列入 KEV，暂无公开的在野利用证据；影响面限于已认证且具备 Streamers、Profile 权限的用户，需配合录制结束这一时序条件。

items.why_it_matters: 拥有主播与资料权限的低权限已认证用户即可借助恶意用户名，在录制结束时以 Liquidsoap 服务账户身份执行任意命令，实现从 Web 账号到宿主系统的越权与横向移动。CVSS 8.8 且利用条件明确，自托管电台场景中该类后台账号通常较易获得。

items.title: AzuraCast before 0.23.8 contains a DQL injection vulnerability in the sortOrder API parameter of AbstractSearchableListAction.php. Attackers can inject arbitrary DQL expressions...
items.summary: AzuraCast before 0.23.8 contains a DQL injection vulnerability in the sortOrder API parameter of AbstractSearchableListAction.php. Attackers can inject arbitrary DQL expressions through the sortOrder parameter to extract sensitive database information including user credentials and station settings.

llm_summary.summary_zh: CVE-2026-100847 是 AzuraCast 在 0.23.8 版本之前存在的一个 DQL 注入（Doctrine Query Language 注入）漏洞，位于 AbstractSearchableListAction.php 所处理的 sortOrder API 参数中。AzuraCast 是一款开源的、可自托管的网络电台管理与流媒体编排平台，其后台与 API 大量依赖 Doctrine ORM 进行数据库查询；列表类接口通常允许调用方通过 sortOrder 之类的参数指定排序字段甚至排序表达式。该组件在拼接排序条件时未对用户输入做充分的校验与白名单约束（例如未限定为预定义的字段枚举），导致攻击者可以把任意 DQL 表达式注入到最终执行查询的排序子句中，从而改变查询语义，使原本仅用于返回列表数据的接口变成可读取任意数据的信息泄露通道。根据官方描述，攻击者可借此读取数据库中的敏感信息，包括用户凭据（账号口令哈希等认证材料）以及电台（station）配置项，而攻击者并不需要预先获得任何账号或交互权限。CVSS 3.1 评分为 7.5，向量为 AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N，即远程、低复杂度、无需认证、无需用户交互，可造成高度机密性影响，但完整性（I）与可用性（A）影响均为无——这与“注入被限制为读取型、无法直接改写或删除数据”的特征相符。厂商已在 0.23.8 版本中修复该问题，因此 0.23.8 之前的版本均被视为受影响版本。目前该 CVE 未列入 CISA KEV，来源数据中也没有在野利用（exploit_in_the_wild / known_exploited）标记，EPSS 数据缺失，故尚无量化证据表明其已被实际利用；但由于无需认证即可远程触发且直接指向凭据泄露，攻击面与潜在收益都很可观，仍应视为高优先级修复项。
llm_summary.why_it_matters_zh: 无需认证的远程攻击者即可通过排序参数注入 DQL，直接读取用户凭据与电台配置，机密性影响为高；修复版本明确（升级至 0.23.8 及以上），且互联网暴露的自托管实例常疏于加固，应优先处置。
llm_summary.impact_zh: 攻击者可绕过接口预期语义，从数据库读取任意可见数据，重点是用户账号凭据（含口令哈希）与电台设置等敏感配置；该类凭据一旦泄露，可能被用于横向登录、进一步接管平台或复用至其他系统。本漏洞不影响数据完整性与服务可用性，但其机密性破坏面大，且受影响实例若未打补丁将持续暴露。

items.why_it_matters: 无需认证的远程攻击者即可通过排序参数注入 DQL，直接读取用户凭据与电台配置，机密性影响为高；修复版本明确（升级至 0.23.8 及以上），且互联网暴露的自托管实例常疏于加固，应优先处置。

items.title: In Google fuse-archive versions prior to 1.24, an attacker who can prepend a directory to PATH or write a malicious binary to an attacker-controlled or writable directory appear...
items.summary: In Google fuse-archive versions prior to 1.24, an attacker who can prepend a directory to PATH or write a malicious binary to an attacker-controlled or writable directory appearing in PATH can hijack the execution pathway. This allows the attacker to execute arbitrary local code under the security context of the user running the fuse-archive process. The issue was partially mitigated in version 1.22 and fully resolved in 1.24 via refined selective PATH filtering.

items.summary: A vulnerability was identified in ООО НПО Ритм GEOritm up to 2.45.1. This affects an unknown part of the file /restapi/objects/obj-groups of the component REST API. Such manipulation of the argument objectId leads to missing authentication. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. Upgrading to version 2.46 is able to mitigate this issue. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component. The vendor confirms: "In August 2026, NPO Ritm received an official vulnerability notification from the Russian Federal Service for Technical and Export Control (FSTEC Russia). The vulnerability was registered under identifier BDU:2026-11235. Following our internal investigation, we confirmed the vulnerability and implemented the necessary security fixes. The vulnerability has been fixed on our hosted GEO.RITM server at geo.ritm.ru. The fix has also been included in GEO.RITM version 2.46, which is already being distributed to our customers."

items.summary: Nezha is a server and website monitoring tool. In versions >= 2.2.11 and < 2.3.1, the service sentinel worker (service/singleton/servicesentinel.go) contains an incomplete fix for a previously reported nil dereference denial of service (GHSA-qjpp-gffx-2wm9). The 2026-07-21 fix re-validated the service lifecycle under serviceResponseDataStoreLock but reused an already-captured, now stale reporter pointer and never re-validated the server, and that lock does not guard ServerShared. An authenticated user with the member role who owns an agent can issue a concurrent server delete (POST /api/v1/batch-delete/server) for their own server to win the race window, causing the worker to dereference a missing entry in the server list snapshot. Because the sentinel workers and the gRPC server have no recover()/recovery interceptor, the resulting panic is unrecovered and crashes the entire instance. This is fixed in version 2.3.1.

items.summary: Nezha versions 2.0.10 through 2.3.2 use a restricted HTTP client to validate user-configurable notification and DDNS webhook URLs, but the denylist did not cover IPv6 transition ranges — specifically the 6to4 prefix 2002::/16 and the local-use IPv4/IPv6 translation prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48. Because such addresses satisfy Go's netip.Addr.IsGlobalUnicast check, the URL validator accepted them. An authenticated user able to configure a webhook may be able to cause the dashboard to issue requests to an otherwise restricted IPv6 endpoint, but only where the dashboard's network provides unusual or non-standards-compliant routing for these transition ranges; no direct path to an IPv4 metadata, loopback, or private-network HTTP request has been demonstrated. The issue is fixed in version 2.3.3 (commit d1fcde8e), which blocks both prefixes.

items.title: python-utcp (pip package utcp-http) before 1.1.12 does not verify whether tool URLs declared in a hand-written UTCP manual point at the agent's own loopback interface when that ...
items.summary: python-utcp (pip package utcp-http) before 1.1.12 does not verify whether tool URLs declared in a hand-written UTCP manual point at the agent's own loopback interface when that manual is discovered from a remote, non-loopback origin. Because ensure_secure_url intentionally permits loopback HTTP for local development and native manuals bypassed the loopback check performed by the OpenAPI converter, an attacker who can serve a UTCP manual that a victim registers can cause the client to issue requests to services bound only to 127.0.0.1 on the victim host and have the response bodies returned to the caller (server-side request forgery). The http, sse and streamable_http protocols are all affected. items.summary: Fleet-maintained app install and uninstall scripts for macOS are generated from Homebrew cask metadata. In manifests generated before 2026-08-19, the script generator escaped this metadata at some interpolation sites but not all of them, so cask metadata containing shell metacharacters (for example $(...) command substitution) could be carried into scripts that execute as root on managed macOS hosts. An attacker who could land crafted metadata in an upstream Homebrew cask — without needing any Fleet credentials — could achieve arbitrary command execution as root on managed macOS hosts that install or uninstall the affected Fleet-maintained app; exploitation required the crafted metadata to pass both upstream Homebrew cask review and Fleet's review of the automated ingestion pull request. The fix (fleetdm/fleet#51324) landed in Fleet's ingestion pipeline on 2026-08-19 so that all manifests generated on or after that date escape cask metadata at every interpolation site; because manifests are generated centrally and distributed as pre-built content, remediation applied to all deployments with no customer action, and the code fix is included in Fleet v4.92.0.

items.summary: Parse Server is an open-source backend server. In versions >= 9.0.0 < 9.10.1-alpha.10 and >= 8.0.2 < 8.6.91, the code-based authentication adapters (GitHub, Google Play Games, Instagram, LINE, LinkedIn, Microsoft, QQ, Spotify, WeChat, Weibo) verify the client's authorization code with the external provider on signup and on provider linking, but not when authentication data is supplied together with a username and password on the login endpoint. As a result, a low-privileged authenticated user can attach an arbitrary, unverified provider identity to their own account without the provider ever being contacted, spoofing an external identity toward application logic that trusts the linked provider ID. An attacker can also pre-hijack accounts: by claiming the provider ID of a victim who has not yet linked that provider, the victim's later legitimate sign-in with that provider resolves to the attacker's account. Only deployments configuring one of the affected code-based auth adapters are impacted. Versions 9.10.1-alpha.10 and 8.6.91 fix the issue by running the adapter's credential verification on the login and challenge endpoints and rejecting a provider identity already linked to another user. As a workaround, disable the affected code-based auth adapters.

items.title: The account recovery (password reset) functionality in the vulnerability-lookup web application contains a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the consumptio...
items.summary:
The account recovery (password reset) functionality in the vulnerability-lookup web application contains a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in the consumption of single-use recovery tokens. The original implementation verified the token nonce against the stored digest and then consumed (cleared) it in separate database operations. Two concurrent HTTP requests presenting the same valid recovery token could both pass the verification check before either transaction committed, allowing both to set their own password on the target account. The last transaction to commit overwrites the first, enabling an attacker who possesses a valid recovery token to replace the legitimate user's password with one of their choosing.

A secondary defect in the same endpoint (confirm_account) allowed a valid recovery link to be used to set an empty or trivially short password (e.g., three characters). The view handler performed only a manual equality comparison between the two password fields and never invoked the form's validation logic, bypassing the intended minimum-length and complexity constraints.

The affected component is the user account recovery endpoint (/user/confirm_account/<token>) and the associated token verification and consumption logic in the User model (website/models/user.py) and the view layer (website/web/views/user.py).

items.title: MatchTrustedPeer ignores the public key used, leading to forged CA clones passing verification. Affected builds are any that enable the macro WOLFSSL_TRUST_PEER_CERT and load CA...
items.summary: MatchTrustedPeer ignores the public key used, leading to forged CA clones passing verification. Affected builds are any that enable the macro WOLFSSL_TRUST_PEER_CERT and load CA certificates with wolfSSL_CTX_trust_peer_cert() or wolfSSL_trust_peer_cert(). The peer must know the certificates being loaded to either of those APIs to take advantage of the issue. When OPENSSL_COMPATIBLE_DEFAULTS is also defined this widens the affected API to include all CA certificate loading. Both macros are defined when using autoconf builds such as (nginx, haproxy, stunnel, wpas, apache httpd, hitch, bind, rsyslog, ffmpeg, all, distro). When the certificate is listed as a trusted peer certificate the issue previously allowed for a malicious (D)TLS server to bypass authentication once knowing which CA’s the client would accept. This also affects mutual authentication cases where the client knows which CA’s the server has loaded. If building with any of these configurations and using (D)TLS where the loaded CA’s could be known and authentication of the peer is desired, users should either: update to the latest wolfSSL version, apply the fix patch, or use the configure flag --disable-openssl-compatible-defaults and not load CA’s with wolfSSL_CTX_trust_peer_cert() or wolfSSL_trust_peer_cert() to mitigate the issue.

items.summary: In wolfSSL versions 5.7.2 through 5.9.2 there is a client-side implementation flaw in RFC 6961, multiple OCSP response stapling, which can lead to certificate forgery. When a wolfSSL client enables OCSP stapling with the HAVE_CERTIFICATE_STATUS_REQUEST_V2 feature and calls wolfSSL_UseOCSPStaplingV2(ssl, WOLFSSL_CSR2_OCSP_MULTI, options), the client accepts any certificate in the peer's chain as a certificate authority without verifying that the certificate is actually authorized to act as one. This means that an attacker who possesses any certificate that chains to a CA trusted by the client (along with its private key) can forge certificates for arbitrary identities that will be accepted as valid by the client. The end entity certificate of the server is stored in the persistent trust store, affecting subsequent connections that reuse the context even when OCSP multi usage is not employed. Found by internal wolfSSL testing.

items.title: Without NO_SESSION_CACHE_REF, wolfSSL_get_session() does not return a session object but a ClientSession reference of the form {row, index, hash(sessionID)} into the process-glo...
items.summary: Without NO_SESSION_CACHE_REF, wolfSSL_get_session() does not return a session object but a ClientSession reference of the form {row, index, hash(sessionID)} into the process-global SessionCache, and ClientSessionToSession() validates it against that hash alone. Because the TLS 1.2 session ID is chosen by the server and sent in clear, AddSessionToCache() matches any other server's session on the same ID and overwrites the client-side entry with that server's master secret, cipher suite and version, while the handle continues to resolve; nothing on the write path compares the peer, the application's server ID or the WOLFSSL_CTX. Resuming through the handle then produces an abbreviated handshake in which no Certificate message is sent, so neither chain verification nor wolfSSL_check_domain_name() runs, and the attacker is accepted as the original server for the whole of that connection. Affected builds are those leaving NO_SESSION_CACHE_REF, NO_SESSION_CACHE, NO_CLIENT_CACHE and TITAN_SESSION_CACHE all undefined, which includes a plain ./configure, --enable-opensslextra and --enable-opensslall; fifteen integration options define NO_SESSION_CACHE_REF and are therefore not affected, among them --enable-all, --enable-distro, --enable-curl, --enable-nginx, --enable-haproxy, --enable-stunnel, --enable-wpas and the rest of the OPENSSL_COMPATIBLE_DEFAULTS family, and --enable-leanpsk, --enable-leantls, --enable-lowresource and --enable-tinytls13 disable the cache outright. The application must use the legacy reference flow, wolfSSL_get_session() or SSL_get_session() followed by wolfSSL_set_session(); wolfSSL_get1_session() returns the session object itself and is not affected, nor are wolfSSL_SetServerID() lookups. Only TLS 1.2 and below and DTLS 1.2 and below are reachable, since TLS 1.3 and ticket resumption with an empty ServerHello session ID both use a client-chosen cache key. The poisoned entry lives in the process-global cache, so it crosses WOLFSSL_CTX boundaries and persists until the entry is evicted or the session times out, 500 seconds by default. Releases v5.3.0 through v5.9.2 are affected; the fix adds a per-write generation counter to the cache and raises WOLFSSL_CACHE_VERSION from 2 to 3, so a cache persisted by an older build is rejected by a fixed one.

items.title: Under WOLFSSL_SMALL_CERT_VERIFY, ProcessPeerCertParse() runs the certificate signature check separately from the parse to keep peak memory down, then merges the two results, but...
items.summary: Under WOLFSSL_SMALL_CERT_VERIFY, ProcessPeerCertParse() runs the certificate signature check separately from the parse to keep peak memory down, then merges the two results, but it merged the signature result back only when the parse returned 0, so any parse error hid it. ParseCertRelative() reaches its validity-date, name-constraint and critical-extension checks only after ConfirmSignature() has passed, so splitting the signature check out inverts the precedence that makes "override date errors" a sound policy, and ASN_SIG_CONFIRM_E is never surfaced anywhere. The attacker needs no key material from the real PKI and no CA compromise: a self-made certificate carrying the expected subject name, the trusted CA's subject as its issuer, arbitrary bytes where the signature goes, a validity window in the past and the attacker's own key pair is sufficient. Affected builds define WOLFSSL_SMALL_CERT_VERIFY, which is off by default, is not set implicitly by any platform or preset header, and is not reachable from any CMake option; the autotools routes are --enable-lowresource, --enable-leantls, --enable-tinytls13=cert and --enable-tinytls13=mutualauth, and examples/configs/user_settings_embedded.h reaches it through WC_CFG_SMALL_CERT_VERIFY, which ships as 0, while neither --enable-all nor --enable-distro enables it at all. The application must additionally install a verify callback through wolfSSL_CTX_set_verify() or wolfSSL_set_verify() with WOLFSSL_VERIFY_PEER that returns 1 for ASN_BEFORE_DATE_E or ASN_AFTER_DATE_E; wolfSSL ships this exact shape as myVerify() in wolfssl/test.h under VERIFY_OVERRIDE_DATE_ERR, which examples/client -D selects. An application with no callback, or whose callback returns preverify for date errors, still fails the handshake, and wolfSSL_CertManagerVerifyBuffer() and wc_CheckCertSignature() report ASN_SIG_CONFIRM_E correctly in the same binary. TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 are affected in both directions, and DTLS reaches the same function; where the forged certificate is a chain certificate the callback's consent causes it to be cached in the WOLFSSL_CTX certificate manager, so an exposed deployment must restart the context or the process rather than merely reconnect.

items.summary: In MONAI 1.6.0, PersistentDataset (monai/data/dataset.py) explicitly rejects the combination track_meta=True with weights_only=True, forcing users who cache MetaTensors (the default tensor type in MONAI >= 1.0) to run torch.load(hashfile, weights_only=False). Related cache helpers in monai/data/utils.py also call pickle.loads on cached content and derive cache keys with hashlib.md5. As a result, a local user with write access to a shared or world-writable cache_dir (e.g. /tmp/monai_cache, HPC scratch, ~/.cache/monai) can place a malicious pickle file that is deserialized the next time another user's MONAI pipeline reads the cache, resulting in arbitrary code execution in that user's context. All released versions of the monai pip package are affected; no patched version is available as of the advisory.
